fact: What happens once a UK play is made: how often a production recoups or a run is extended, box office per performance or week

sources.title: SOLT & UK Theatre: Theatre in the UK 2026 (published 11 March 2026), pp. 16-17
sources.said: The West End generated record revenue of £1.084 billion in 2025 (up 4.1%) with 17.64 million attendances (up 3.16%). However, the number of performances grew slightly faster, rising by 3.26%. … average occupancy eased slightly to 84%. … The majority of tickets were sold at £56 or below, with more than a quarter under £35. … A West End play typically requires £1–2 million in upfront capital, with fixed weekly running costs of £120,000–£200,000 before royalties. … A West End musical may cost £3–10 million or more, with fixed weekly costs of £300,000–£400,000 … a production typically receives 70–81% of face value, and close to 60% where tickets are sold through third-party agents. A large musical may therefore need to gross £500,000 or more per week simply to break even. Even successful plays often recoup only late in their run, if at all.

The engine could run a play week by week (gross = seats x occupancy x price x the 70-81% share, less the weekly running cost and the 8% royalty) and recoup when cumulative net covers capital, from these figures, the occupancy draw being the game's own (told).
